        Serie A is back this weekend, with Lazio and AS Roma the standout teams of the season so far, while Inter and AC Milan have had some ups and downs. Elsewhere, Juventus and Napoli are still in trouble but at least seem to be getting a little better than in previous weeks. This weekend features some key Serie A games, such as Inter vs. Genoa and Como vs. Juventus on Sunday. Let's take a closer look at what to watch for on Matchday 13: the game, the player and the story you need to know.Game to watch: Como vs. JuventusComo will host Juventus on Sunday for a key Serie A game as the two teams are currently fighting for a spot in the top four. Both sides also played in Europe this week, and Como beat AEK Athens in the Champions League. Under the guidance of Cesc Fabregas, Como have emerged as one of the biggest surprise teams of this European campaign. Currently sitting third in the league-phase standings, behind only Real Madrid and PSG, the Italian side has had an impressive start to its Champions League journey. With four wins in five matches, they have secured at least a playoff place, while a top-eight finish is now a realistic ambition in what is their first-ever Champions League campaign.Player to watch: Lautaro MartinezInter captain Lautaro Martinez is finally back after missing the last month of action and also scored in the latest Champions League match against Stuttgart at San Siro after coming on off the bench.         The 2027 college football season is set to start with a bang. Texas Tech and USC have announced a non-conference matchup at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Aug. 27, 2027.The Red Raiders and Trojans have only met three times in their history, with the most recent matchup coming in the 1995 Cotton Bowl. USC has won all three matchups, but Texas Tech will try to get on the board while picking up a quality win to start next season.
Trojans coach Lincoln Riley has plenty of connections to Texas Tech. Riley worked there as an assistant under Mike Leach from 2003-09. After starting as a student assistant, Riley climbed to the role of wide receivers coach before taking an offensive coordinator job at East Carolina.
Depending upon how things shake out in the offseason, there's a good chance both teams will be ranked inside the preseason top 25 when they take the field in Las Vegas.In past years, this matchup would land on Week Zero, but the NCAA has made changes to the FBS calendar that will go into effect on Jan. 1. Week 1 has been moved up one week, meaning fans won't have to wait quite as long for the official start of the college football season.
All that said, Texas Tech and USC have bigger fish to fry this season. The Red Raiders punched their ticket to the Big 12 Championship Game with a win over TCU on Thursday night, and the Trojans have their rivalry game against USC coming up on Saturday afternoon. The Trojans could keep their biggest rival out of the Big Ten Championship Game while getting to nine wins.

        Survivor Series has been defined by two eras: the original event, which ran from 1987 to 2021, and the WarGames period. This year, those eras collide at Daikin Park in Houston. WWE superstars might want to take tips from the Houston Rockets because teamwork is the name of the game. Three team-based matches are set for this year's show, including two WarGames matches and a traditional five-on-five Survivor Series match. The match taking up the most time on WWE programming is the gang war between The Bloodline and 946. Roman Reigns and Royce Keys' factions will settle matters inside the massive WarGames cage.The traditional format commonly features five superstars on each team. It's an elimination match in which all members of a team must be pinned, submitted, counted out or disqualified before a victor is crowned. The format returns to its namesake event for the first time in five years, pitting Team USA vs. Team Mexico. "The American Nightmare" Cody Rhodes captains Team USA, with CM Punk, Je'Von Evans and LA Knight as his first recruits. Team Mexico captain Rey Mysterio counters with the Lucha Bros, Penta and Rey Fenix.

In addition to the three Survivor Series matches, a world title match is scheduled. Liv Morgan will defend the women's world title against Becky Lynch, looking to put a capstone on their ongoing feud. 
Plus, WWE legend The Rock is scheduled to make a return on Saturday to celebrate the 30th anniversary of his WWE debut. Many are speculating what it could mean, with many thinking he could factor in some way to the Bloodline saga.Take a look below at the confirmed matches for Crown Jewel. The new group has been taking the fight to Reigns' family, generally getting the better of them. However, Fatu's return on Nov. 9 set the stage for a finale in the most appropriate environment.
Survivor Series Match -- Team USA (Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Je'Von Evans, LA Knight and Seth Rollins) vs. Team Mexico (Rey Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix, Dragon Lee and El Grande Americano): Rhodes and Mysterio will captain their respective teams for Survivor Series. The match has largely been built on respect and national pride. Punk offered his services to Team USA, which Rhodes gladly welcomed. However, neither team wanted to take Dominik Mysterio. Newly-minted world tag team champions Penta and Evans were put into an awkward situation after accepting invitations to represent their respective countries. Fortunately for Penta, he has a familiar face in his corner, his brother, Fenix. The drama intensified with with Rhodes' final pick for Team USA, which was a returning Seth Rollins and that infuriated Punk and Punk remains distrustful of his old rival.Women's World Championship -- Liv Morgan (c) vs. Becky Lynch: Lynch wants a "fair fight" for the women's world championship. Morgan reclaimed the title at Money in the Bank in a triple threat match involving Lynch, though Lynch wasn't pinned. They subsequently wrestled for the title on Raw. Lynch won by disqualification, meaning the title didn't change hands. Lynch has a reasonable claim to the title and plans to settle the matter in Houston.WarGames Match -- Charlotte Flair, Stephanie Vaquer, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, and Bayley vs. Fatal Influence (Jacy Jane, Fallon Henley, and Lainey Reid) and The Baddies (Jade Cargill and Michin): This match has been brewing for months.         The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2-3 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples. Just recently, for instance, the New York Mets landed the biggest fish in the pond by signing ace Tarik Skubal to a record contract. Not long after, the Chicago Cubs fortified their rotation with Trevor Rogers and their outfield with Teruaki Sato. Freddy Peralta (Baltimore Orioles) and Jazz Chisholm Jr. (Toronto Blue Jays) are also off the board, among others. More are likely to come before the lockout arrives. Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Yankees going for Morejon
The New York Yankees have yet to make a headline-grabbing move this offseason, but that might soon change. The Yankees are prioritizing lefty reliever Adrian Morejon, the New York Post reports. Morejon, who doesn't turn 28 until February, is coming off a standout season with the San Diego Padres and has been a force in their bullpen for the last three years. Morejon's deep repertoire and elite velocity make him a candidate to convert to a starting role, but the Yankees would presumably have him in mind as their next relief ace. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cardinals looking for veteran rotation helpThe St. Louis Cardinals, who are still emerging from a rebuild, aren't going to be major players on the market this winter, but they might be looking to repeat one of their approaches from last offseason. Last winter, they inked right-handed starter Dustin May to a one-year pact and were able to flip him to the Milwaukee Brewers for an impressive return leading up to the trade deadline. Lead decision-maker Chaim Bloom might be looking to do that again, The Athletic reports. While there are no specifics in the report, some available names who might check the Cardinals' boxes include Casey Mize, Shota Imanaga, and Shane Bieber, among others. If those efforts don't bear fruit, the Cardinals could instead target middle-relief help. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    D-backs add Kona TakahashiThe Arizona Diamondbacks have agreed to terms with right-handed starting pitcher Kona Takahashi out of Japan on a one-year contract, the New York Post reports. Takahashi, who turns 30 in February, was posted by the Seibu Lions last offseason but didn't fetch a deal until this time around. Across parts of 12 seasons in NPB, Takahashi pitched to a 3.30 ERA with 984 strikeouts and 465 unintentional walks in 1,337 ⅓ career innings. With Arizona, Takahashi could be a back-end starter or provide additional bullpen depth. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Orioles want lefty armsThe Orioles have already added Peralta to the front of the rotation, but they may not be done pursuing arms. Specifically, they'd like to add lefties to their rotation and their bullpen, The Athletic reports. At present, the fringy Cade Povich is the only left-hander in the rotation, and while the bullpen presently has a pair of lefties on the depth chart, neither Josh Walker nor Grant Wolfram is a potent option.

Curry is making 'good progress' ahead of his re-evaluation next Wednesday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:58 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Golden State Warriors announced that Stephen Curry will be sidelined through at least next Tuesday as he continues to rehab the oblique abdominal tear he sustained on Nov. 11 against the Houston Rockets. That means he will miss at least the Warriors' next two games, home dates against the Los Angeles Clippers and Utah Jazz. The Warriors, who were blasted by the Damian Lillard-less Portland Trail Blazers on Friday and have lost five of their last seven following an eight-game win streak, say Curry is making "good progress" as he has started on-court workouts. Curry will be re-evaluated next Wednesday, the day after the Utah game. By that point, the Warriors, now 10-9, will be into a lighter stretch of schedule as the NBA Cup knockout rounds play out. If you look at their schedule right now, they don't have a game between Dec. 1 and Dec. 12, but two games will be added during that window for all teams that didn't advance out of the group stage. Still, that's only two games over a 10-day stretch. It's a good way for Curry to ease back if he is cleared to play after next Wednesday, which sounds like a distinct possibility. Curry was initially slated to miss at least two weeks. He's already passed that line, but Warriors coach Steve Kerr says Curry has been in the gym every day and "everything's on schedule."
Whenever Curry gets back, it won't be soon enough for a Warriors team that has looked completely lost without him. It's been even worse than losing six of seven sounds. 
After the first game following Curry's injury, a bashing at the hands of the Spurs, Yaxel Lendeborg, who'd been living the high life playing alongside Curry through the first three weeks of his career, described the feeling as "helpless," and he's not far off. It's literally two different teams. Before Curry's injury: The Warriors ranked first in 3-point percentage, second in offensive rating, points per game and both true and effective FG%, and fifth in net rating. Since Curry's injury: The Warriors rank dead last in points per game, offensive rating and both effective and true shooting, and second-to-last in 3-point percentage and net rating. Entering Friday, the Warriors were outscoring opponents by 13.3 points per 100 possessions with Curry on the court, which would rank as a top-five offense, per Cleaning the Glass. Without him, that number falls to minus-8.5 with what would rank as a bottom-five offense. That's more than a 20-point swing. The numbers match the eye test. With Brandon Williams also out over this stretch, the Warriors lack a true leverage creator, and as such, quality shots are hard to come by. They've been held under 100 points in six of their seven games since Curry went out. They've lost five of those games by at least 20 points and have been outscored by a total of 111 points. 
Still, these next two games against the Clippers and Jazz, both at home, are more than winnable even without Curry, and the Warriors need to take advantage. They gave themselves a cushion to absorb this Curry absence with their 8-3 start, but they're down to 10-9 now and in danger of having to bring Curry back to a below-.500 team.

title: Pat Kelsey's superb Players Era run in Vegas makes Mark Pope's rocky Kentucky tenure look that much worse - CBS Sports

body:
Kentucky is in crisis; Louisville is embarking on a renaissance. Friday night provided the greatest gap yet since these coaches were hired
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 28, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:40 am ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        LAS VEGAS — In the early spring of 2024, one of college sports' best rivalries got a burst of intrigue when Louisville hired Pat Kelsey and Kentucky hired Mark Pope less than two weeks apart. It was the first time in 94 years that the Bluegrass State blood rivals made coaching moves in the same offseason. Neither coach was the first, second or even third choice for the job.Pope was the Pollyannaish, beloved captain of one of the best college basketball teams ever, the 1995-96 Kentucky Wildcats led by Rick Pitino. Kelsey was a welterweight ladder-climber who doggedly worked his way up in the business under the initial tutelage of the late, great Skip Prosser. Which one would ultimately prove to be the better pick? Well, 33 months after they were brought in to course-correct two of college hoops' most important programs, Friday night provided a clear answer.Kelsey is lapping Pope. Louisville (6-1) is winning the race and the gap is increasing. Kentucky (4-3) is losing and the fan base is infuriated, with Pope's coaching reputation hitting its latest low in the Wildcats' 73-71 home overtime loss to Wichita State. UK didn't have its best all-around player (Malachi Moreno), but that shouldn't matter. Kentucky is supposed to be beating mid-major opponents in Rupp Arena by double digits the majority of the time.

        
            
                How Mark Pope's inexplicable overtime coaching blunders doomed Kentucky in rock-bottom loss to Wichita State
                
                    David Cobb                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Other than getting blown out by Wichita State (which hasn't made the NCAA Tournament since 2021) it's hard to imagine a more disastrous way to lose than how Kentucky did itself in on Friday. The team blew a 14-point advantage on its home floor on the 50th anniversary of the first Wildcats game at Rupp Arena — and did so with a coaching blunder that will be constantly referenced by millions of Kentucky fans for as long as Pope is the coach.After Kentucky gave away a big lead and failed to win in regulation, the Cats predictably found themselves losing footing in overtime to a Shockers team that smelled blood. Down 73-71, Kentucky players opted against fouling Wichita State with less than 25 seconds remaining, a boneheaded decision that somehow didn't cripple UK because the Shockers stalled their way into a shot-clock violation. Then came the decision that may mark the beginning of the end for Pope in the weeks/months to come. Because the clock was stopped on the turnover and Kentucky was awarded the ball with five seconds remaining, the inbounder can't move while out of bounds. 
In a dereliction of duty, Pope forgot about the rule, which some UK fans immediately ruled as grounds for dismissal. A design for Alex Wilkins to pass along the baseline to Mason Williams — with Williams hopping out of bounds to receive the pass — was immediately whistled. Incredibly, Wichita State again gave Kentucky a chance when the Shockers couldn't inbound the ball after the turnover, but the ensuing scramble on Wichita State's turnover led to a missed final shot from Kentucky.  Absurd sequence, yet so fitting for the quagmire this opening month has been for Pope's program.
Kentucky fans rained down boos — for minutes — as Pope left the arena's view. He is probably never living that sequence down."That is 100% on me," Pope said afterward. "Somehow that changed to a live ball in my mind and I messed that up. And it's really costly. That's a tough one to carry as a coach for sure."Not one player or assistant realized the gaffe as the play was being drawn up in the huddle? How? 
The 4-3 start is Kentucky's worst since the bizarre COVID year of 2020-21 under John Calipari, which triggered the slow-boil end to his time in Lexington three years later. Pope won't be given the grace of a long-tail exit. Things have to change in the weeks ahead, or else this will get too ugly to tolerate. The 54-year-old is without question sitting on the hottest seat in the sport.
        
            
                Mark Pope buyout, contract details: How much it would cost Kentucky to fire coach after loss to Wichita State
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Kentucky's loss to Wichita State was made all the worse because of the comparisons to what Louisville is doing this season. The teams played their games concurrently Friday night, two contests separated by 1,686 miles that ended in drastically different ways. Kentucky is in crisis; Louisville is embarking on a renaissance.The No. 25 Cardinals are way better than that ranking, a reality that will be reflected in the next AP Top 25. That's because Louisville smoked No. 9 Tennessee 84-64 in their Players Era 16 winners' bracket matchup. It was U of L's third consecutive win over a ranked team this week, following Thanksgiving night's theatrical win at the buzzer against No. 13 St. John's and Tuesday's 72-64 rumble against No. 5 Texas Tech. 
Whereas Kentucky is plummeting in every computer metric, the Cardinals continue to rise while achieving things this program hasn't accomplished since the peak of Pitino's tenure well over a decade ago. For one, Louisville defeated three ranked teams in a row away from home in non-con play for the first time since the 2012 NCAA Tournament. The Cardinals' shredding of Tennessee was also the program's first 20-plus-point win away from home against a top-10 team since the 2013 Elite Eight vs. Duke, the most recent year Louisville won the national title.U of L also became only the fifth team in the history of the sport to beat three top-15 teams in a four-day span, per ESPN. The win against the Vols was all the more notable after Tennessee crushed Louisville and Kelsey the past two seasons. "Twice they beat us like we stole something in every facet," Kelsey said, adding he had "PTSD" when he looked at the bracket and realized playing Tennessee a third year in a row was possible. 
Then his team went out and dropped 84 points on a Volunteers group that was giving up just 58.4 points per game heading into Friday night, the third-lowest mark in D-I. Those kinds of results aren't happening at Kentucky, which has a 2-7 record in its last nine nonconference games against high-major teams.All five Cards starters hit double figures Friday — and the team-high was 17 off the bench by Seth Trimble, who's looking like one of the most valuable transfers of the 2026 cycle after averaging 24.7 points on 58.5% shooting and 4.0 rebounds and assists in the past three games against top-15 competition."We're just a team that truly believes in each other," Trimble said. "Like, I believe in [my teammates] with all of my heart. I believe in my head coach with all of my heart, and everybody shares that with each other. Our first practice after we lost to Memphis, we had a good practice and everybody after the practice, everybody's just like, 'We're back.' Everybody's smiling. Everybody's, 'We're back. Louisville basketball is back.' Like, we're good. We just have that belief in each other, and I just think it's contagious and it spreads." 
The opposite is playing out at Kentucky. You won't find quotes like that as often.These two programs, which rank at the top of the sport in spending and might not be separated by more than $1 million in payroll this season, are somehow a chasm apart in on-court performance. Money doesn't guarantee you anything, a lesson that a few teams seem to learn every year. This is the second straight season for Kentucky to face that fact."We are still so early in this season," Pope said. "I think this team has a great upside. We just have to continue to get better. I clearly have to continue to get better. That's where we are. We are not scared of that. It's just the job."
Meanwhile, here's Kelsey from Thursday night: "In this NIL world, and sometimes it's me, me, me, and it's my social media clicks and how much money I make. This team is special. Like there is no, there's nothing. They're a group of dudes that just care about each other and just go to work like pros every single day. We don't have parent problems. We don't have agent problems."Trimble, Adrian Wooley, Flory Bidunga and Alvaro Folgueiras were all singing the same tune. Carry a pro mindset, treat your teammates as brothers, keep everyone invested and don't let the trust crack. Louisville hasn't felt or looked like this in a long time."This is a really important year for a lot of our guys in the locker room, we don't want to waste it because it's a really big chance to make history," Folgueiras said.
The season is young, but Louisville is obviously one of the three or four biggest winners of the opening month. Kelsey spent well north of $20 million on this roster, and the massive investment looks like it's going to lead to a breakthrough. His approach to coaching is definitely not for everyone; Kelsey admitted to me in years past that he's a different bird and he can't change the essence of who he is or how he operates. But the everyday message seems to be landing properly with this group."As Seth mentioned, what's the secret sauce? I mean, I think two things. One, our program is centered on the most powerful force in the universe, and that's love," Kelsey said. "Selflessly loving the guy next to you and sacrificing for the guy next to you. Not about your social media hits or NIL or whatever it is. It's busting your butt to not let your buddy down. We call it the power of the unit." Speaking of units, Louisville just upped its stacks, increasing one of the biggest budgets in college basketball. The win over Tennessee got the program $500,000 in additional NIL opportunities. On Saturday night at Michelob Ultra Arena, Kelsey's Cardinals will face Creighton in the Players Era 16 championship game for an additional 500K.As Louisville's going for 7-1 and striving to break into the top 10, Mark Pope will be at home, trying to figure out a way to avoid getting blown out at undefeated and No. 2 Virginia on Tuesday. Ten days later, the biggest day on the calendar will arrive. Louisville heads to Rupp Arena on Dec. 12. It will be the most important game of Pope's Kentucky tenure. Practically speaking, Kelsey will be playing with house money that night. Pope could well be coaching for his job.
